Stated Claim / Post Context:
Sound Transit installs mesh cages to stop fish deaths under I-90 light rail

Sound Transit said Thursday it’s installing 13 mesh tube cages to wrap around a device believed to be killing fish.

Actual Article Body:
Sound Transit said Thursday it’s installing 13 mesh tube cages to wrap around a device believed to be killing fish.

In August, Sound Transit CEO Dow Constantine announced that an unusual number of fish, including salmon, had been discovered on the bottom of Lake Washington near the 2 Line’s Crosslake Connection on the I-90 floating bridge.

The suspected culprit: underwater wires, called anode strings. The wires are connected to floating pontoons that emit electrical currents that prevent the steel and concrete from corroding.

The agency believes that fish are being electrocuted when they swim by the wires. Last week, divers added the new cages to over a dozen of the pontoons to prevent any more fish deaths. The cages are made of off-the-shelf supplies commonly used in aquaculture, the agency said, and were designed with fisheries staff from the Muckleshoot Indian Tribe and the Washington State Department of Fish and Wildlife.

Cameras were also installed inside the mesh tubes to monitor any fish activity. If these first 13 cages work as planned, Sound Transit said it will add them to all 136 pontoon anode strings on the bridge.
